ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PRC: Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2019); Partnership Enterprise Law of the PRC (2006 Amendment); Regulations of the PRC on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Order No. 746); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Anti-Money Laundering Law of the PRC (as amended). Hong Kong SAR investor side: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) Part 5A on significant controllers register; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615); United Nations Sanctions Ordinance (Cap. 537).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Business License for Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Market Supervision Administration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize at a Chinese notary public, then obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or a provincial foreign affairs office. If the destination jurisdiction is not a Hague Apostille Convention member, do not use Apostille; instead obtain consular legalization at the destination jurisdiction's consulate. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance from registration and tax authorities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAMR / State Taxation Administration local office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the certificate at a Chinese notary public, then apply for an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or authorized provincial foreign affairs office. For a non-Apostille destination, apply for consular legalization at the destination consulate after MFA authentication; never combine Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing FIP formation and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or authorized governing body of the Hong Kong SAR investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute before a Hong Kong notary public, then obtain an Apostille from the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. If the destination is not an Apostille Convention member, use consular legalization at the destination consulate in Hong Kong or through the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs; the Apostille and consular legalization routes are mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Foreign-Invested Partnership Agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All founding partners of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sign and notarize before a Chinese notary public, then obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or authorized local foreign affairs office. If the destination state is not an Apostille Convention party, obtain consular legalization at the destination consulate; do not apply Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank of the investing entity or of the Foreign-Invested Partnership after preliminary KYC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize at a notary office in the jurisdiction of the issuing bank, then obtain an Apostille if the destination is an Apostille Convention member, or consular legalization at the destination consulate if the destination is a non-member. The two authentication pathways are strict alternatives and must never be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be performed on all founding partners, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and counterparties before formation and on a rolling basis after formation against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, PRC MOFCOM unreliable entity and export control lists, and Hong Kong sanctions lists under Cap. 537 and AMLO Cap. 615. Enhanced due diligence must be applied to all politically exposed persons, including mainland China PEPs, their immediate family members, and close associates, with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence required. For TikTok creator payout and Wise B2B payment rails, the FIP must screen beneficiaries and linked accounts for sanction exposure, PEP status, adverse media, and negative OFAC information. All screening hits, rejections, risk ratings, and clearing decisions must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR Enterprise Name Reservation System and National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; for the Hong Kong investor, the Hong Kong Companies Registry Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a Foreign-Invested Partnership in mainland China must be in standard simplified Chinese characters and must follow the four-tier structure: administrative division plus distinct trade name plus industry or business characteristics plus legal form indicator. The legal form indicator must clearly reflect a partnership, e.g., limited partnership. English or romanized names are not registered as the legal name; an English translation may be used in contracts and bank documentation but has no statutory name protection. Hong Kong investor documents may be in English, but all Chinese name clearance filings must conform to PRC transliteration, pronunciation, and character standards, and any Hong Kong company name should be transliterated phonetically and consistently.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving an electronic rejection from the SAMR name-reservation portal, the applicant should download the rejection notice and reference number, identify the conflicting token or structural defect, correct the proposed name, and resubmit within the original reservation application. If the applicant believes the rejection is unlawful, file a written administrative reconsideration application with the next-higher market supervision administration within 60 days from the date of the rejection notice, attaching the rejection notice, proposed name structure, partnership agreement, and legal arguments. If administrative reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may institute an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within six months. Legal counsel should be engaged to address recurrent rejections due to sensitive or identical trade-name conflicts.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and commercial mailbox arrangements are generally rejected for an active Foreign-Invested Partnership in the creator/MCN agency industry. PRC market entity registration rules require a fixed and legitimate business premises, the tax authorities require a physical address with lease agreement and proof of use, and banks uniformly require on-site inspection before account opening. A pure registered-agent or virtual office address will cause rejection of the business license, tax registration, and bank account. A co-working space may be acceptable only if the FIP itself holds a dedicated desk or office lease, the space is identifiable, and utility and occupancy records confirm actual business operations. For TikTok MCN operations with staff and creators, a physical office with signage, policies, and records is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical on-site inspections: (1) lease agreement in the FIP's name; (2) landlord identity and property ownership certificate; (3) utility invoices matching the address; (4) office signage matching the registered name; (5) staff presence and attendance records; (6) accounting books, invoices, and bank statements; (7) creator contracts and MCN operating agreements; (8) tax filing receipts. Quantified risk: Medium, approximately 30% likelihood of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months for an active digital-economy entity, and higher if the registered address is shared, residential, or inconsistent with the stated business scope.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Hong Kong Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38), Sections 3, 4, 6, and 7; Limited Partnerships Fund Ordinance (Cap. 637), Sections 5, 8, 10; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), Sections 5 and 6; Companies (Fees and Charges) Regulation (Cap. 622K); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 3, 4, and 28; Implementing Regulations of the Foreign Investment Law, Articles 12 and 16.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry; Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department; Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China (MOFCOM) through the Foreign Investment Comprehensive Management System; State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statement of Particulars for Limited Partnership (Cap. 637) or Partnership Registration Statement (Cap. 38); Business Registration Application Form IRBR1; Certificate of Foreign-Invested Partnership Filing with MOFCOM.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for Hong Kong SAR; the Partnership Ordinance imposes no minimum paid-up capital. Partnership contributions are determined contractually. No blocked escrow account is required by Hong Kong law. If the Chinese Foreign-Invested Partnership branch is separately registered in mainland China, applicable local registration may require a nominal declared contribution, but no statutory minimum applies to pass-through partnership structures.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BOARD OF THE FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP, adopted in writing in accordance with the Partnership Agreement and the Limited Partnerships Fund Ordinance (Cap. 637) of the Hong Kong SAR. The undersigned, being all the initial governing board members and authorized managing partners, hereby resolve as follows: 1. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Partnership in Hong Kong SAR shall be located at the address designated by the licensed corporate service provider, and that such address shall be filed with the Hong Kong Companies Registry and the Inland Revenue Department. The managing partner is empowered to execute any Change of Registered Office Notice and to engage a commercial registered office provider. 2. CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS AND SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED, that the initial capital contributions set forth in the registered Partnership Agreement and Statement of Particulars are hereby ratified and accepted; that each partner shall contribute cash or in-kind consideration as set out in the contribution schedule; that the capital accounts shall be maintained in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles; and that no distribution or withdrawal of capital shall occur except as permitted by the Partnership Ordinance and the written unanimous consent of all partners. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Partnership shall establish operating accounts with licensed banks in Hong Kong, including but not limited to DBS Bank (Hong Kong) Limited, HSBC, and Standard Chartered Bank, and with Wise B2B as an electronic money institution for cross-border creator payouts. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the managing partner, together with any one designated officer, shall have authority to open, close, and operate bank accounts; to deposit and withdraw funds; to sign checks, wire instructions, and electronic payment orders; to execute foreign exchange transactions; and to enter into banking agreements, all subject to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) and the Partnership's internal approval matrix. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENT: RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed as statutory officers: the individual named in the Statement of Particulars as the Managing Partner; the individual named as the Compliance Officer with responsibility for AML/CTF and licensing filings; and a licensed solicitor or corporate service provider as the Partnership Secretary. Each officer shall hold office until resignation, removal by resolution, or dissolution. 5. FILING AND COMPLIANCE: RESOLVED, that the Managing Partner and Compliance Officer are jointly directed to complete all filings with the Hong Kong Companies Registry, the Inland Revenue Department, MOFCOM, SAMR, and any other regulatory body, including the Business Registration Certificate, the Limited Partnership registration, and the Foreign-Invested Partnership information report. Such officers are authorized to retain counsel, pay all statutory fees, execute all declarations, notarize and apostille documents, and obtain all necessary approvals to commence operations. 6. GENERAL AUTHORITY: RESOLVED, that any one authorized officer may execute and deliver all agreements, instruments, and certificates necessary to carry out the foregoing resolutions, including the TikTok Creator Payout agreements, Wise B2B terms, and any intellectual property licensing or management agreements. These resolutions shall be effective immediately and shall remain in full force until revoked by subsequent resolution. Certified copies shall be provided to the Partnership's bankers, auditors, legal counsel, and regulators.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Structure Clearance and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOFCOM Foreign Investment Comprehensive Management System; Hong Kong Companies Registry through the Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS); State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) local counterpart.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a preliminary Foreign-Invested Partnership information report with MOFCOM to confirm that the ISIC 7310 agency and creator management activities are outside the foreign investment negative list. Submit the draft partnership agreement, all partners' certificate of incorporation or identity documents, and a business scope description. Concurrently conduct a name search with the Hong Kong Companies Registry via ICRIS for the proposed English and Chinese name of the partnership. Ensure that the name is not identical or similar to existing entities. If required by MOFCOM, submit a notarized Chinese translation of the foreign partner's documents. Obtain a written negative-list clearance or pre-filing confirmation before proceeding to registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Partnership Agreement
Certificate of incorporation of the corporate partner, if any, or passports of individual partners
Notarized Chinese translations of foreign documents, if required
Proposed business scope referencing ISIC 7310 and NAICS 541810
Foreign investment negative list compliance statement
Name reservation application with three alternative names
Power of attorney appointing the Hong Kong corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOFCOM issues a query, the applicant shall submit a written explanation and amended documents within 15 business days. If the Hong Kong name is rejected, select the next alternative and re-file immediately. If a negative-list concern is raised, seek a written advisory opinion from MOFCOM or revise the business scope to exclude restricted sub-activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hong Kong Partnership Registration and Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry; Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form LP1 (Statement of Particulars for Limited Partnership) under the Limited Partnerships Fund Ordinance (Cap. 637) or the appropriate partnership registration form under Cap. 38. Provide the partnership name, registered office address, general partner's details, limited partners' details, capital contribution schedule, and business nature. After registration, submit Business Registration Application Form IRBR1 with the IRD and pay the prescribed fee and levy. Both filings can be made online through the e-Registry portal with the applicant's recognized digital certificate. The partnership agreement must be executed by all partners and notarized if required by Chinese partners. Obtain the Certificate of Registration and Business Registration Certificate, and retain certified copies for bank account opening.
required_dossiers: Duly completed Form LP1 or partnership registration statement
Business Registration Application Form IRBR1
Partnership Agreement signed by all partners
Certified copies of identity documents of general and limited partners
Registered office address consent letter
MoFCOM pre-filing clearance or negative-list confirmation
Proof of payment of registration fees
Digital certificate of authorized signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry suspends the application for incomplete details, resubmit the corrected form within 5 business days and pay any applicable reinstatement fee. If the IRD questions the business nature, submit a supporting description detailing creator incubation, talent agency, advertising, and digital content monetization. If the name is rejected, file an appeal with the Registry's Name Review Committee or adopt an alternative name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Banking Mandate Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed banks in Hong Kong (e.g., DBS, HSBC, Standard Chartered); Wise B2B as an electronic money institution; Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) AML/CFT supervisory framework.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a partnership bank account in the exact registered legal name. Present the Certificate of Registration, Business Registration Certificate, Partnership Agreement, and the certified first board resolution authorizing signatories. Complete the banking mandate specifying signature thresholds and dual-control requirements. Provide source of funds and source of wealth statements for all partners, a business plan covering TikTok Creator Payout flows, projected monthly volumes, and counterparty due diligence. For Wise B2B, upload the same entity documents and complete platform verification, including beneficial ownership declarations. Ensure that all payment rails are compliant with the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance. Obtain a bank reference letter if required by future commercial counterparties.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of the partnership
Business Registration Certificate
Partnership Agreement and Statement of Particulars
Certified first board resolution
Passports and proof of residential address of all signatories
Business plan and cash flow forecast
TikTok Creator Payout agreement or MCN contract list
Beneficial ownership declaration
Source of wealth documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide supplemental responses within 5 business days. If the application is rejected, request the written reason, remedy the deficiency, and apply to an alternative licensed bank. For Wise B2B failure, furnish tax identification numbers, additional proof of physical office, and a resolved business profile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Chinese Foreign-Invested Partnership Filing and Post-Registration Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOFCOM Foreign Investment Comprehensive Management System; State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) local office; State Taxation Administration; local Public Security Fire Rescue authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Hong Kong registration is complete, file the final Foreign-Invested Partnership information report with MOFCOM within 30 days, reporting the Hong Kong entity as the foreign investor. If the partnership operatives in mainland China directly, complete the SAMR registration for a Foreign-Invested Partnership branch or establish a wholly domestic entity; obtain the Unified Social Credit Code. Register with the local tax authority for income tax and VAT, and apply for the appropriate preferential pass-through treatment if eligible. Report beneficial owners to the SAMR anti-money laundering registry. If no physical operation is conducted in mainland China, the Chinese filing is limited to MOFCOM information reporting. For all mainland office leases, obtain a fire safety inspection certificate before operations.
required_dossiers: Hong Kong Certificate of Registration and Business Registration Certificate
Statement of Particulars
First board resolution
Notarized and apostilled Partnership Agreement
Foreign investor passport or corporate certificate
Lease agreement and landlord ownership proof
Tax registration forms
Beneficial owner declaration form
Fire safety self-inspection and building certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOFCOM flags the filing for insufficient substance, submit a supplementary letter with contracts, bank statements, and engagement letters. If SAMR requires corrections, execute an amending agreement and resubmit. If the fire safety inspection fails, remedy the specified deficiencies and schedule reinspection within 10 business days. If the taxation authority challenges pass-through status, file an administrative review or provide additional economic substance documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - The entity operates exclusively as a digital creator agency and multi-channel network (MCN) under ISIC 7310. No physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing activities are conducted.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - No industrial operating permit is required for pure digital/consulting services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - No Environmental Impact Assessment is mandated for office-based MCN operations under the Hong Kong Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499) or the PRC Environmental Impact Assessment Law.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - No EIA report, environmental registration, or pollution permit is required because the enterprise generates no industrial discharges, hazardous waste, or stationary emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable for industrial emissions. General office waste must be disposed of through licensed waste collectors under the Hong Kong Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354); in mainland China, office domestic sewage must connect to municipal sewers compliant with the Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard (GB 8978-1996).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial fire permits. However, the Hong Kong office must obtain a Fire Services Installation (FSI) certificate under the Fire Services Ordinance (Cap. 95) confirming that fire alarms, emergency lighting, and extinguishers meet code. In mainland China, obtain the Fire Inspection Acceptance Certificate from the local fire rescue authority before occupancy. Occupational safety compliance under the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) requires a general risk assessment, first-aid provisions, and emergency evacuation plan. No special civil defense permit applies.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; electronic filing portal: eTAX (https://www.etax.gov.hk). The Business Registration Office forms part of the IRD for Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Confirm the Hong Kong business registration obligation under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310). An entity described as a Foreign-Invested Partnership, where constituted as a partnership in Hong Kong, is treated by the IRD as a partnership. Step 2: Prepare the partnership deed or limited partnership agreement, passports or foreign registration certificates of all non-resident partners, proof of a Hong Kong registered office or service address, and, where the non-resident partners have no Hong Kong fixed place of business, an appointment letter for a Hong Kong authorised tax representative. Step 3: If the arrangement is a limited partnership, first register with the Companies Registry under the applicable Hong Kong limited partnership legislation, then file Form IRBR 1 with the Business Registration Office through the eTAX portal or in person, together with the prescribed fee. Step 4: Obtain the Business Registration Certificate and the partnership Tax File Number; the Business Registration Number serves as the Hong Kong TIN. Because Hong Kong has no VAT or GST, no separate VAT ID is issued and no VAT registration is made. Step 5: After registration, the IRD issues profits tax returns to the partnership; however, the partnership itself does not pay profits tax on the aggregate profit. Under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), each partner is separately assessable on their share of the partnership profit sourced in Hong Kong.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Hong Kong has no check-the-box election and no hybrid mismatch entity classification election. The IRD applies the partnership substance: partnerships are tax-transparent for Hong Kong profits tax, and partner-level territorial source rules under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) govern assessability.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Not_Applicable - Hong Kong has no VAT, GST, or general sales and use tax. Excise duty is chargeable only on a limited class of dutiable commodities under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (Cap. 109).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable. There is no indirect tax registration threshold in Hong Kong because no general indirect tax exists. Business registration under Cap. 310 is triggered by carrying on business in Hong Kong, not by turnover, and does not impose VAT or GST obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Hong Kong does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory e-invoicing, or anti-fraud digital stamping for indirect taxes. The IRD requires the maintenance of adequate records and books of account sufficient to verify assessable profits. Cross-border electronic invoicing is a commercial requirement from counterparties, not a Hong Kong statutory tax clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. Hong Kong does not levy VAT or GST on exports or domestic supplies; therefore there is no 0% export VAT rate, no statutory export zero-rating claim, and no VAT refund mechanism. A Hong Kong MCN agency may invoice TikTok and creator clients without Hong Kong indirect tax. For customs purposes, only dutiable commodities require export duties or non-direct tax declarations; digital creator services do not pass through customs. If the Hong Kong entity's profits are not sourced in Hong Kong, the IRD applies territorial source principles, but this is a profits tax issue and not an indirect tax zero-rating matter.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: No indirect-tax export substantiation bundle applies in Hong Kong because no VAT or GST zero-rating claim is possible.

Where physical goods or dutiable commodities are moved through Hong Kong customs, the required trade documents are: Electronic Export Declaration filed under the Import and Export (Registration) Regulations (Cap. 60E) through the Trade Single Window; Commercial Invoice; Packing List; Bill of Lading or Air Waybill; and any applicable destination-country import certificate.

For cross-border service fee repatriation, a bank may request the signed MCN or service agreement, TikTok Creator Payout or Wise B2B transaction statements, the FIP's commercial invoice, and a payment receipt.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Not applicable to export VAT zero-rating because Hong Kong does not grant zero-rating relief. However, if the partnership makes false or inaccurate trade declarations, the Import and Export Ordinance (Cap. 60) and the Customs and Excise Service Ordinance (Cap. 342) provide fines and imprisonment for false declarations. If the partnership underreports Hong Kong-source assessable profits in the partners' returns, the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) authorises the IRD to assess additional tax up to three times the tax undercharged plus a fine, and to prosecute for fraudulent tax acts; the assessment period extends to six years for ordinary negligence and ten years for fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and its State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for the China-resident Foreign-Invested Partnership; Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the separate monetary authority for the Hong Kong structuring and treasury vehicle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The China-resident FIP operates within a stringent capital-account control environment. The renminbi is convertible on current-account items for genuine trade and cross-border service transactions once the bank has completed authenticity and conformity review, but capital-account flows remain governed by SAFE registration and operational boundaries. The Hong Kong leg enjoys free convertibility under the Linked Exchange Rate System, but the binding constraint for the FIP is the PRC Foreign Investment and Foreign Exchange administration framework. The FIP must open a SAFE-registered FDI foreign exchange capital account to receive the Hong Kong partner's capital contribution; funds cannot be freely used or settled into RMB unless the capital account payment is aligned with the registered commercial purpose and supported by contracts, invoices, or audits as applicable. Profit remittance to the Hong Kong partner is a current-account distribution and requires audited financial statements, final tax settlement certificates, partnership profit-distribution resolutions, and Chinese bank verification under SAFE's current-account payment rules. Conversely, service income received from TikTok or overseas clients can be retained in foreign currency or voluntarily settled into RMB after the bank reviews the underlying service contract and platform statements. No surrender margin is imposed on the Hong Kong vehicle, but the PRC FIP must participate in the nationwide trade monitoring and declaration system for every cross-border receipt or payment. Thus the practical FX environment is a hybrid: full external convertibility at the Hong Kong treasury level and prudential, documentary-driven convertibility at the China FIP level.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For the PRC FIP, export and cross-border service proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated to a domestic foreign-currency current account; after authenticity review, the FIP may retain the foreign exchange or voluntarily settle into renminbi. There is no fixed percentage surrender requirement under the current Chinese framework, but the bank and SAFE require the proceeds to be credited only after trade or service documentation is matched, and retention is subject to the enterprise's declared foreign-currency account status. For the Hong Kong treasury vehicle, no surrender obligation exists; proceeds may be held in any freely convertible currency with no prescribed timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account
Multi-Currency Operational Account with SAFE-Eligible Current Account Settlement
RMB Basic Deposit Account and Foreign Currency Current Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Export Proceeds Retention Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low / Not viable for the China-resident FIP. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise B2B, Revolut, Airwallex, or Payoneer do not hold a Chinese commercial banking licence and cannot provide renminbi current accounts, SAFE foreign-exchange registration, or capital-account services to a mainland-resident Foreign-Invested Partnership. The FIP must use a licensed Chinese commercial bank for foreign currency receipt, settlement, and capital injection. The Hong Kong parent may use a licensed EMI or Money Service Operator for offshore creator payouts outside China, provided the EMI is registered with the Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department as a Money Service Operator or is an HKMA-licensed institution; unlicensed offshore EMIs are not acceptable as a primary clearing rail. Therefore, the TikTok creator payout rail should be split: Hong Kong-based payouts via an authorised institution or licensed MSO, and all China-sourced amounts via a domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The PRC FIP's managing partner or duly authorised operator must normally appear physically at the bank's corporate department to complete KYC, seal registration, and face-to-face interview. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not available for the first-time opening of the FIP's FDI capital account because the bank must verify the original SAFE FDI registration, the partnership registration certificate, and the statutory chops. A Power of Attorney granted by the foreign managing partner to a China-based authorised individual may be accepted after notarisation in the grantor's location, translation into Chinese, and legalisation or apostille where applicable, but the attorney must appear in person with the original instrument. For the Hong Kong treasury account, a physical or supervised video-call interview with the authorised signatory and beneficial owners is required under HKMA guidance; remote onboarding is possible only where the bank offers a licensed digital onboarding channel and the corporate structure is simple, which is not the case for a multi-level FIP with overseas partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through partnership structure with multiple foreign and Hong Kong beneficial owners triggering beneficial-ownership opacity under PBOC Beneficial Owner Identification Measures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original notarised FIP partnership agreement; FIP business registration certificate and SAFE FDI Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate; complete corporate and beneficial-ownership organogram with all individuals holding over 25% partnership interests; duly translated passports and residence permits; 12-month source-of-wealth bank statements and net-worth declarations; independent legal opinion confirming the FIP is valid under PRC Foreign Investment Law; written AML attestation from the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: TikTok creator payouts to numerous non-resident and short-form video creators raising layering, fragmentation, and potential illicit-flow concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed creator representation agreements with full legal name, address, tax ID, and bank details for every creator; TikTok and MCN platform performance and payout statements reconciled to the bank payment schedule; commission calculation model; creator KYC and sanctions-screening records; evidence that each payout is consistent with a genuine service contract; withholding tax rationale and tax vouchers; internal transaction monitoring policies with threshold alerts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border service flows between the China FIP and the Hong Kong partner with risk of over/under-invoicing, transfer mispricing, or disguised capital movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany service agreements with precise scope, deliverable matrices, pricing methodology, and intellectual-property clauses; transfer pricing documentation prepared under PRC and HK rules; tax invoices or valid e-invoices; evidence of actual service performance including server logs, creative assets, campaign reports, and attendance records; audited unit economics and benchmark comparability report; external accountant's capital-verification or payment-matching report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP exposure, or negative reputational hits involving the Hong Kong partner or ultimate foreign partners within the TikTok and MCN supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent sanctions and PEP screening reports covering all directors, partners, authorised signatories, and beneficial owners; negative media and litigation search results from mainland Chinese, Hong Kong, and foreign registries; source-of-wealth declarations supported by bank statements, property contracts, tax assessments, or corporate sale documents; certificate of incumbency and current search reports from the Hong Kong Companies Registry; legal opinion on sanctions and anti-bribery compliance; confirmation that no target is subject to Chinese or international banking restrictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from the Hong Kong partner must be routed by SWIFT MT103 with the registered overseas partner as the sole remitter and the FIP's SAFE-registered FDI capital account as beneficiary. The payment instruction must carry the SAFE transaction declaration code for inbound direct investment in a foreign-invested partnership, the SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration Code from the FDI registration certificate, the FIP's full Chinese and English names, and the reference of the partnership's capital contribution schedule. The receiving bank will validate the remitter against the registered partner list, credit the funds to the foreign-exchange capital account, and then require the FIP to provide underlying contracts, capital contribution notices, and if required by the bank a PRC certified accountant

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership Annual Return (Form LP-2) under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance Cap.352
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry, Registrar of Companies (Hong Kong SAR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of registration of the limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Each general partner is liable on conviction to a fine of up to HKD 50,000 (approx. USD 6,410) plus continuing daily default fines; persistent non-filing may trigger gazetted administrative strike-off or deregistration by the Companies Registry after warning notices.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate Renewal under the Business Registration Ordinance Cap.310
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department (Hong Kong SAR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal on or before the expiry date of the existing Business Registration Certificate, or within one calendar month after expiry while the late renewal is accepted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts a surcharge equal to 10 percent of the outstanding business registration fee and levy (minimum HKD 300); continued non-renewal is an offence, and unpaid fees and penalties are recoverable by the Inland Revenue Department as a civil debt.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Profits Tax Return (Form BIR52) under the Inland Revenue Ordinance Cap.112
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Profits Tax Unit (Hong Kong SAR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month from the issue date of the return; for a 31 December financial year end the customary extended deadline is 15 August of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Inland Revenue Department may raise a best-of-judgment assessment under section 59(3); late or incorrect filing may attract penalties up to HKD 10,000 plus additional tax of up to three times the undercharged tax, and willful evasion may lead to fines and imprisonment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Annual Return (Form BIR56A and Individual Employer Returns BIR56B) if the partnership employs staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Employer Returns Section (Hong Kong SAR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month from the issue date of the Employer's Return, normally issued in early April for the tax year ended 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in estimated assessments, a fine of up to HKD 10,000 per offence, and further daily default fines under the Inland Revenue Ordinance Cap.112.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Hong Kong limited partnership is not automatically audited solely because of entity form, but a statutory independent audit is required where: (1) the Inland Revenue Department expressly requires audited financial statements with the partnership Profits Tax Return, which is the standard administrative position where annual gross income exceeds HKD 2,000,000 (approx. USD 256,410) or where losses or group relief are claimed; (2) the vehicle is constituted as a Limited Partnership Fund under the Limited Partnership Fund Ordinance Cap.637, which requires audited financial statements by a certified public accountant; (3) any Hong Kong corporate partner or underlying Hong Kong company breaches the Companies Ordinance Cap.622 'small private company' thresholds of annual revenue exceeding HKD 10,000,000, total assets exceeding HKD 10,000,000, or more than 50 employees, and is not dormant or validly exempted; (4) a mainland Chinese subsidiary or branch meets PRC statutory audit triggers under PRC Accounting Law, generally annual turnover above RMB 30 million, total assets above RMB 40 million, or more than 200 employees; and (5) lenders, investors, or the MCN platform require audited consolidated financial statements as a contractual condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), fully converged with IFRS; eligible private entities may apply HKFRS for Private Entities; any PRC consolidated subsidiary or branch must prepare PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE) for local statutory purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing for a pure limited partnership. However, if the partnership operates through or includes an Hong Kong company/corporate general partner, the Significant Controllers Register under the Companies Ordinance Cap.622 must be kept current and updated within 15 days of any material change. The limited partnership itself must notify the Companies Registry of changes in partnership particulars, including transfers of partnership interests, within the statutory notice window, normally 7 days, and annual confirmation is embedded in the Form LP-2 annual return. If any PRC foreign-invested equity or partnership interest transfer occurs within the group, the underlying PRC foreign investment information report must be filed within the 30-day statutory reporting window.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (General Partners, Limited Partners and Capital Contribution Records)
Register of Significant Controllers / Beneficial Owners (where Cap.622 applies)
Register of Directors / Authorised Representatives (for any corporate general partner)
Register of Charges / Mortgages and Guarantees
Statutory Minute Book (partnership resolutions, admissions, withdrawals and capital changes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$400 - US$1,200 per annum for a Hong Kong registered office and registered agent or corporate secretarial service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500 - US$18,000 per annum depending on turnover, number of creator agreements, group complexity and consolidation requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% for unincorporated partnership profits tax; 16.5% for corporate taxpayers
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Two-tiered profits tax: first HK$2,000,000 of assessable profits are taxed at 7.5% for unincorporated business (8.25% for corporations), with the balance taxed at 15%/16.5%; territorial source principle exempts profits derived outside Hong Kong; 100% tax deduction for qualifying research and development expenditure; foreign-sourced income not assessable; no capital gains tax, no dividend withholding tax

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: BIR52 - Partnership Profits Tax Return; e-filed via the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department (IRD) eTAX portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within 1 month from the date of issue (usually 1 April for accounts ending 31 March); unless an extension is granted, e.g. professional firms may obtain extension to 15 August for fiscal periods ended 31 March

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Part A - Name and Business Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the partnership and its Hong Kong Business Registration (BR) certificate number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact BR number as shown on the certificate. If the partnership is not resident in Hong Kong, state 'Non-HK resident' and include a Hong Kong address for correspondence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Part A - Principal Business Activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of the main economic activity (ISIC 7310: advertising and multi-channel network agency).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Clearly describe the actual services (creator incubation, MCN talent representation, advertising brokerage). Avoid generic descriptions that may trigger an IRD source-of-profits enquiry.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Part B - Income and Expenses (Profit & Loss Account)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed statement of gross receipts, allowable expenses, and net profit or loss for the accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all income arising in or derived from Hong Kong, including global TikTok creator commissions remitted to the HK bank. Where the income is partly from non-HK sources, make an appropriate apportionment and submit a claim for offshore sourcing with supporting permanent establishment (CIGA) documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Part B - Adjusted Assessable Profit or Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-adjusted profit after adding back non-deductible expenses and claiming capital allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Knock back fines, private expenses, depreciation (in lieu of capital allowances), and any sum not incurred in the production of assessable profits. Non-resident partners may use this figure to allocate their distributive share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Part C - Allocation of Profits among Partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Percentage profit-sharing ratio and the amount of assessable profit attributed to each partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List every partner, including non-resident foreign-invested partners from China (CN). For non-residents, show HK ID/TIN or foreign tax number. The partnership must attach a schedule showing each partner's share; if any partner is exempt, attach supporting evidence (e.g. family office concession, fund exemption).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Part D - Election for Personal Assessment or Other Reliefs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Election options and claims for deductions such as charitable donations, patent box reliefs, or double taxation relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners cannot normally elect personal assessment unless they are individuals. Claim foreign tax credit relief against HK tax on the same profits using the IRD's Form 28 (or via the DTA) if the profits have also been taxed in Mainland China. Attach the China tax payment certificates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (IRO) s. 80(2), an incorrect return without reasonable excuse attracts a fine of up to HK$10,000 and a further fine of treble the tax undercharged; fraudulent evasion under s. 82 may result in a fine of HK$50,000 plus treble tax and imprisonment for 3 years. Late filing may incur a fine of HK$10,000 plus a daily default penalty of HK$300 per day.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Hong Kong does not impose dividend withholding tax on distributions to partners, including non-residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because Hong Kong levies no domestic withholding tax on outbound profit distributions, no DTA relief procedure is required for dividends paid by the HK partnership to a PRC investor. However, if the partnership derives income from Mainland China through a PE or is deemed a PRC-resident enterprise, the PRC-HK Double Tax Arrangement (DTA) may grant a withholding tax reduction on dividends/interest/royalties paid by a PRC entity to the partnership. To claim the reduced rate, the HK partnership must obtain a Hong Kong tax residency certificate from the IRD (Form IR1313A), provide an exceptional circumstance declaration (if required), and prove beneficial ownership through: (i) a board of directors or governing partners, (ii) substantive business premises and employees in Hong Kong, (iii) a shareholders/partners registry, and (iv) a written declaration from the ultimate beneficial owner. The certificate will then be sent to the PRC withholding agent to apply the 5% dividend rate (if holding ≥25% capital) or 10% otherwise.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Hong Kong has no statutory withholding tax on royalty or interest paid to non-residents. Where the payer is a PRC company and the HK recipient is a beneficial owner, the PRC-HK DTA reduces PRC withholding tax on interest from 10% to 7% and on royalties from 10% to 7% (subject to the anti-abuse clauses and the required procedural filings with the PRC tax authority, including the Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under IRD's Transfer Pricing Rulings and the Income (Amendment) Ordinance 2018, a HK taxpayer must prepare a Master File and Local File if it meets all of the following: yearly total turnover ≥ HK$200 million and controlled transaction amounts exceed HK$5 million for property transfers, or HK$1 million for financial transactions, intangibles and services. Even below these thresholds, the partnership must maintain contemporaneous evidence for any cross-border related-party transactions (e.g. parent MCN revenue split with TikTok, inter-company creator contracts) to support arm's length pricing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Hong Kong does not have BVI-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the source rule requires that the core income-generating activities (CIGA) of the MCN agency (contract execution, creator management, negotiation, billing and active decision-making) be performed in Hong Kong to justify the 'carrying on of business in Hong Kong' for profits tax. A pure booking shell that remotely directs operations from Mainland China will fail the source test, and the IRD may deem profits as taxable in Hong Kong, apply the anti-abuse rule under s.61A to disregard artificial transactions, and, where DTA relief is claimed, deny treaty benefits under the principal purpose test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Profits Tax Return Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting from BIR52 commissions received from TikTok's creator payouts and Wise B2B settlement accounts, or claiming inflated management fees to reduce assessable profits to nil in Hong Kong.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue Ordinance (IRO) s.82: criminal liability for knowingly making a false return; fine of HK$50,000, treble the amount of tax undercharged, and imprisonment for up to 3 years. IRO s.80(2) for an incorrect return without reasonable excuse: fine up to HK$10,000 plus treble tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: For a limited partnership, the general partner (GP) is deemed the responsible person and may be individually assessed. A court may order the GP/directors to restore the undercharged tax from their personal assets; IRD may seek a Mareva injunction to freeze assets, and an asset freeze order can ban the individual from leaving Hong Kong (travel restriction) until the tax is settled. Convictions carry deportation or extradition risk under mutual legal assistance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Maintain Proper Accounting Records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to retain books, contracts, bank records, and creator payout records for at least 7 years, contrary to IRO s.51C; using offshore shell accounts without an audit trail.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRO s.51C(2): on conviction, a fine of up to HK$100,000 plus a daily fine of HK$1,000 for each day the offence continues (in practice, courts order imprisonment for up to 6 months where the fine is unpaid).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The GP, managing partner, and any appointed representatives are jointly and severally liable for the partnership's record-keeping failures. Civil liability includes the reversal of accounting evidence and reconstructive tax assessments; persistent non-compliance can support a finding of fraudulent trading under the Companies (Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance, leading to disqualification from holding an office in any HK company for up to 15 years and an order to contribute personal assets to cover the tax shortfall.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the MCN agency as a Hong Kong pass-through partnership while all substantive decisions and economic activity (creator sign-up, commission negotiations, TikTok ad contracts, and intellectual property licensing) take place in Mainland China, causing profits to be booked in HK and then immediately distributed to avoid both PRC and HK tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRO s.61A (General Anti-Avoidance Rule) empowers the IRD to disregard artificial transactions and re-allocate profits on a reasonable basis; an additional tax assessment of up to 100% of the tax avoided may be imposed under s.82A. In the PRC, similar avoidance provisions (Enterprise Income Tax Law Art. 47) and the general anti-abuse rule (SAT) may recharacterize the arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under principle of piercing the corporate veil, courts may disregard the limited liability structure where the entity is trading fraudulently or as a sham. The GP or directors face personal civil liability for the full tax underpaid, damages for misrepresentation, and criminal charges of conspiracy to defraud the IRD. A travel ban (blacklist) may be issued by the court upon IRD's application for unpaid tax, prohibiting departure from Hong Kong until payment. In serious cases, extradition to Mainland China for tax fraud under the PRC-HK Mutual Legal Assistance Agreement can result in imprisonment of up to 7 years in PRC.
